conflicts.point: Whether antitrust enforcement against cloud-compute partnerships strands vital infrastructure capital or prevents incumbent market locking.

positions.stance: Antitrust enforcement that unwinds equity stakes strands vital capital and freezes energy infrastructure required for modern data center campuses.
Data center capacity runs on regulated utility tariffs and long-term power purchase agreements, so unwinding equity stakes prevents transmission capacity locking.

conflicts.point: Whether pre-deployment safety audits and export controls create an asymmetric compliance burden that harms open-source ecosystems.

positions.stance: Pre-deployment compliance mandates impose asymmetric fixed costs on non-commercial developers, forming a regulatory cartel that freezes open-source ecosystems.
Threshold-gated verification targets centralized cloud infrastructure and high-end clusters without imposing compliance burdens on non-commercial programmers.

verdicts.conflict: Whether antitrust enforcement against cloud-compute partnerships strands vital infrastructure capital or prevents incumbent market locking.
verdicts.rationale: The skeptic position specifies the regulatory mechanisms of utility tariffs and power purchase agreements that govern data center deployment. The accelerationist claim relies on generalized assertions about capital flow without detailing specific project bottlenecks.
verdicts.whatWouldChange: Evidence that data center projects collapse entirely when equity partnerships dissolve, rather than shifting to debt financing or utility-backed power contracts.

verdicts.conflict: Whether pre-deployment safety audits and export controls create an asymmetric compliance burden that harms open-source ecosystems.
verdicts.rationale: National Institute of Standards and Technology evaluations provide concrete performance benchmarks showing open-source competitiveness. The accelerationist counter-claim offers a theoretical argument about regulatory cartels without empirical proof of developer shutdown.
verdicts.whatWouldChange: Comprehensive cost surveys showing that compliance mandates force a measurable percentage of non-commercial developers to abandon open-source projects.
